proposal:
STATUS: nothing here was executed. All traces are hand derivations from the supplied code and may contain slips. No polynomial SAT claim.

1. AUDIT. compression._verify_certificate builds blocks from every original clause, compares each block truth table with its quotient slice, confines used forms to the block support, and checks every entry of P*L=I. I found no unsound path. probe() can only drop input clauses, and only an UNSAT binary quotient is used. Three work findings:
(a) step() calls refute() before elim_plus, so nodes that elim or 2-SAT would decide still pay a full IALH call.
(b) refute() runs HNF on every window, although a table containing a point and all its Hamming neighbours has integer hull Z^s and yields zero rows.
(c) The rank-deficient branch of dual_certificate uses unmodular HNF. Nothing in the code bounds its bit growth, so no per-node polynomial bound is provable yet.

2. EXACT WORK REPAIRS (unimplemented, falsifiable).
LAZY-IALH: run elim_plus first, and call refute(reduced) only when it returns STUCK with a non-binary residual. Given IALH soundness and elim equisatisfiability, sat, peak and layers are unchanged. On my round-86 receipt (layers 2,4,0; 15 calls; 1 refutation) the call count must fall to 7 or 8.
STAR-SKIP: test a centre and its s neighbours first (s+1 UP runs instead of 2^s). On success skip the window; the rows produced are identical.

3. CUBE-LINE LEARNING (CLL): a restricted sound factoring rule with no fresh variables.
A line L={Q_1..Q_r} of consistent, variable-disjoint cubes denotes OR_i AND Q_i.
FOLD: accept L if every transversal clause (one literal per cube) is a clause of F. By distributivity F implies L. Discovery: for seed clause C and literal l, S(l) is the set of l' with C[l->l'] in F, found by hashing C minus one literal. Accept if prod|S(l)|<=m and all transversals are present.
CUT: from L containing Q and a clause C containing the negation of every literal of Q, derive (L minus Q) plus singletons of C minus neg(Q). It is admissible if total cube weight does not increase.
LEARN: a line of singletons of width <=c is an implied clause; add it. F stays equivalent, so SAT answers remain valid.

Neon58 quotient: FOLD gives two lines of four 2-cubes (16 transversals each). Cutting the A-line against P_1j..P_4j keeps weights 8,6,4,2 and yields (b_j OR b_j'); the B-line is symmetric. That is eight binary clauses from 32 cuts. They subsume all 16 positive clauses.

Cost: hashing is O(L*w*log n) bits. Each seed needs one product check of at most m lookups, so the worst case is O(m^2*w*log n). Descents have at most m lines x r cubes x m partner seeds, each at most r steps over at most m candidates. Learned clauses of width <=c number O(n^c), which bounds rounds. So CLL(c) is unconditionally polynomial preprocessing; it bounds nothing about residual search. The certificate per learned clause is L, its transversal index map and the cut list, with checker cost O((prod|Q_i|+r)*w*log n).

4. EXTRAS. Added clauses cannot destroy a fold or a cut partner, so exhaustive bounded descents are monotone under additions. Replacement is different: Neon 91 hides eight positive clauses behind three weaker ones each. By hand, self-subsuming resolution (SSR: a resolvent replaces a parent it subsumes; each step deletes a literal, so at most L steps) restores them. Example: (1,3,6,9,15,16) and (1,-3,6,8,9,15,16) give (1,6,8,9,15,16); with (1,6,-8,9,15,16) this gives (1,6,9,15,16). Prediction: the SSR fixpoint of that 124-clause fixture is exactly the 108-clause Neon58 set.

5. INDEPENDENT-TEST PREDICTIONS. On the exact 16-variable quotient: 2 lines, 8 learned binaries, then root UNSAT with peak 0 and at most one IALH call. The fixture below tests the post-condition on pinned v5 with only the four B-side clauses added. Compression should skip (all_variables_in_odd_blocks) and core should report no_clauses_removed. Root IALH should return an empty_table certificate at window [9,11,13,15] after 24 windows and 336 tuples. With IALH disabled, root elim should still finish: A-variables are pure, and B eliminations are size-nonincreasing (20,19,18,17,16, then 8,4,2).

6. NOT HANDLED.
- Pigeonhole: folds give only lines with one large cube and no cut partner. k-DNF resolution lower bounds for pigeonhole exist in the literature (Segerlind-Buss-Impagliazzo, recalled, not rechecked). The h=4 run has peak 1 and 7-8 calls, so its seconds are per-node IALH cost. Repairs 2 target that; h=5 stays undecided.
- Partners hidden behind non-self-subsuming resolution.
- Near-products missing one transversal.
- Incompatible GF(2) spaces.
missing_theorem:
M1 (soundness; elementary, to be Lean-checked). If every transversal of L is subsumed by a clause of F, then F entails OR_i AND Q_i. CUT preserves entailment. The checker runs in O((prod|Q_i|+r)*w*log n) bit operations.

M2 (exactness of the work repairs). If refute is sound and elim_plus preserves satisfiability, LAZY-IALH returns the same sat, peak and layers as pinned step(). For STAR-SKIP: a table containing t and t+e_i for all i has difference lattice Z^s, so hull_rows returns no rows.

M3 (per-node work). Every step() costs at most p(L) bit operations for a fixed polynomial p. Elim keeps clause count nonincreasing and width <=n, and the IALH caps are constants. The only unbounded part is the unmodular HNF branch of dual_certificate; a bound needs a modular or fraction-free replacement. Given M3, residual work <= p(L)*(1+2*sum over layers of |S_l|) plus pruning. The invariant is frontier area, not peak.

M4 (the real gap). A class theorem: for which CNFs does SSR + CLL(c) + pinned DP leave polynomial frontier area? I have only a hand trace for PT_k without extras. With added clauses the learned binaries persist, but root refutation then depends on the 256-window cap and on canon_plus rewriting. A general M4 would be an automatability statement for a fragment of Res(2). Resolution itself is known to be non-automatable unless P=NP (Atserias-Mueller, recalled). So M4 for all CNF is not weaker than the goal; the honest target is a syntactic class closed under arbitrary clause additions.
self_attack:
1. CLL is restricted Res(2). BDP definitions p-simulate it, and Fable73 twin contraction already covers PT. Its only advantages are no new variables, soundness independent of the rest of the formula, and monotonicity under additions. That may not justify a new component.
2. FOLD finds exact products at a seed. Extracting a maximal sub-product from a partial product is a biclique-type problem with no guarantee from greedy shrinking. One deleted transversal defeats FOLD unless it is subsumed.
3. Weight-nonincreasing descent is a heuristic. Exhaustive admissible lines on PT_k can reach about 4^k = N^2. That is polynomial here, not in general. Beam caps make it incomplete.
4. The fixture is a post-condition, not growth evidence. Its refutation comes from the IALH empty table, so it says little about elim.
5. The SSR prediction is hand-derived. I may have missed strengthenings, and SSR fixpoints need not be unique.
6. LAZY-IALH saves at most about a factor 2 in calls; STAR-SKIP at most 32/6 per window. Neither changes asymptotics, and h=5 may still time out.
7. Recalled lower bounds mean no constant-width cube-line system handles pigeonhole. Counting needs a mechanism other than 5-variable windows.
8. Nothing here is Lean-checked.
mechanism_signature: CLL: FOLD exact product clause blocks into fresh-variable-free Res(2)-style cube lines by distributivity; weight-nonincreasing CUT descents; learn implied clauses of width <=c with enumerative certificates. SSR pre-normalisation against resolution-hidden partners. LAZY-IALH and STAR-SKIP as exact per-node work repairs. Frontier-area work invariant, conditional on bounding HNF bit growth. No polynomial SAT claim.
